item.title: Ficus Exasperata Suppresses Early Events in Colorectal Carcinogenesis by Down Regulating the Expression of Beta-Catenin, Enhancing Adenomatous Polyposis Coli and Boosting the Immune System.
item.description: Wingless (Wnt) signalling is an important evolutionarily conserved signalling pathway in animals that regulates biological processes such as development, cell growth, and differentiation. Abnormalities in the components of the Wnt/β-catenin signalling pathway have been a major cause of cancer, especially in colorectal cancer (CRC). item.title: HAEMATOLOGY, SERUM BIOCHEMICAL RESPONSES AND LIPID PROFILE OF RABBIT DOES FED DIETARY SUPPLEMENTAL LEVELS OF TURMERIC (Curcuma longer) RHIZOME MEAL
item.description: This study was undertaken to examine the haematological characteristics, serum biochemical indices, and lipid profile responses of rabbit does following dietary supplementation with turmeric (Curcuma longa) rhizome meal. A total of twenty-four rabbit does were randomly distributed into four treatment groups comprising six animals each, with each group further divided into three replicates of two does per unit. item.title: Unraveling the plant growth-promoting potential of Bacillus safensis P1.5S through genome analysis
item.description: Plant growth-promoting bacteria have emerged as promising eco-friendly alternatives to traditional agricultural practices. These beneficial microbes promote plant growth through various mechanisms including nitrogen fixation, production of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), salicylic acid (SA), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and antimicrobial secondary metabolites.
